question: Does this function carve out a special case — a branch, flag, sentinel or match arm that handles one kind of input apart — where a deeper model of the thing would make that input an ordinary case?

fine.real_distinction: Every branch separates things that are genuinely different in the domain, each handled as what it is; or the function does not branch beyond guard clauses.

violations.carve_out: A branch exists because the general path cannot take one input or construct: `if is_reduce`, `unreachable!("… must special-case it")`, a sentinel value, a flag or Option field for one caller, an "edge case" or "special case" comment. A model in which that input is an instance of the general case would delete the branch.
violations.exception_to_a_rule: The code or its comment states a principle and an exception to it ("never X, except here"), or reserves something by convention for one purpose.

guidance: Name the deeper model: say what the carved-out case IS, as an instance of the general one ("a loop header is a label", "a temp is a value", "the pool base is a value"), and what deleting the branch would take. Where the ontology defines the term, use its definition.
